prize_parts.citation: for the development of palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, a general method for constructing aryl amines

statement.case_for: I keep B016 as my preferred configuration. Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling is a general method whose impact can be checked in the literature: bulky biaryl phosphine (Buchwald) and hindered trialkyl and ferrocenyl phosphine (Hartwig) ligands made a harsh, narrow transformation predictable on hindered, heteroaromatic and base-sensitive substrates, and the reaction is now routine in medicinal and process chemistry. The mechanism (oxidative addition, amine binding and deprotonation, reductive elimination) is well understood and was worked out in detail by both groups, so the case can be stated in one sentence. Two independent groups developed the catalysts and kept extending them for decades, so the two-name credit is clean. After more than 25 years of use the record is mature, and none of the eight round-1 statements disputes that. The chair's summary shows that no position has five votes yet. I do not think a vote count should decide the science, and I have not found a scientific reason to leave a mature, cleanly attributed method for a candidate that the committee itself describes as maturing.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection, which Xiaodong Zou put directly, is that C-N coupling will be read as completing the 2010 C-C cross-coupling prize instead of opening a new field. I accept that it is a judgement of degree. Priority is also not perfectly clean: Kosugi and Migita's tin-amide chemistry came first, and I limit the credit to Buchwald and Hartwig because the catalytic, general system is theirs. The method has less public reach than the biomedical candidates, and B016 has had the thinnest support of any leading position: in round 1 only Aqvist lists it, as an alternative. If the committee decides that the prize should go to the broadest-supported candidate, B056 is the defensible one, and I would want its citation written narrowly.

responses.point: Zou agrees that Buchwald and Hartwig are a natural pair and that B016 is mature, but worries that a C-N prize would be read as completing the 2010 cross-coupling prize, whereas induced proximity opens a new modality.
responses.response: I take the point as a question of degree, and I think the chemistry answers it only in part. The 2010 prize rested on C-C bond formation (Heck, Negishi, Suzuki). C-N coupling was not a routine extension of that work: the Pd-amido intermediate is prone to beta-hydride elimination and reductive elimination from it is slow, so the problem was solved by ligand design that had no counterpart in the C-C work, and the result opened an entire class of aryl amines that C-C coupling cannot reach. That is a new capability, not a new nucleophile in an old cycle. I also accept that the argument does not make B016 newer than a new modality. We differ on what the prize should weigh: you weigh opening a new field, and I weigh a method that has changed daily practice for 25 years. I would not call your position wrong.

responses.point: Chabes places targeted protein degradation first because induced proximity is a general catalytic tool and the cereblon result explains thalidomide mechanistically, while also saying the PROTAC and glue arms are a judgement call to pair.
responses.response: Your own reservation is the one I find decisive for this year. You say pairing Handa's cereblon mechanism with the engineered PROTAC concept is a judgement call, and you cannot verify the priority record. Zou says the design rules for PROTACs are still empirical, and Brzezinski says reproducibility is strongest on the imid side. If the strong half is the glue mechanism and the PROTAC half is still maturing clinically, a citation that spans both is the least secure part of the prize. I still see the cereblon discovery as a real chemical result, and I rank B056 first among my alternatives. But I do not move my first choice on a trio the proponents say they cannot fully defend, and I do not think a four-member plurality is a replacement for that.

responses.point: Brzezinski prefers B056 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa because the three names map onto distinct, attributable steps, and notes that ternary-complex structures describe the mechanism in atomic terms.
responses.response: I agree that the structural evidence is the strongest argument for B056, and it is more persuasive to me than the number of compounds in trials. Where I disagree is that the three-person limit is workable without a priority ranking. Crews and Deshaies are the concept, Handa is the target, and the omission of Ciulli, whose VHL ligands and ternary-complex work made the design rational, and of Sakamoto, who is on the first PROTAC paper, is a fairness question you also raise. Aqvist, Chabes and Zou raise the same objection. Four members support one trio, but they also give four versions of why it is exposed. I would accept B056 if it is written narrowly, around induced proximity and cereblon and not around clinical outcomes, but I do not yet consider it settled.

responses.point: Aqvist moved B056 to first place and calls the credit split a compromise and not a settled outcome, and he keeps B016 as an alternative.
responses.response: Johan, I appreciate that you list B016 as an alternative, and I agree with your remark that the three-name set splits the PROTAC and glue strands. That remark is why I do not expect the committee to resolve B056 cleanly this round. You also ask that the citation say the concept is general without implying any protein can be degraded. I would add that the same discipline applies to B016: the citation should claim a general method for aryl amines, not all C-N bond formation. On B058, I said in round 1 that I cannot judge simulation as well as the synthetic literature, and I have not changed that. I keep it as an alternative because the credit is clean and the record is long, and I would not oppose it.

uncertainties: Whether the committee reads C-N coupling as a distinct advance after the 2010 C-C cross-coupling prize, or as its completion.

Whether the committee can write a B056 citation that holds the PROTAC and cereblon-glue strands together without a contestable three-person cut, and whether Ciulli or Sakamoto should displace one of the proposed names.
Whether colleagues will accept that a method with limited public reach but 25 years of verified use outweighs a four-member plurality for a modality that has no approved PROTAC drug.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict has arisen since round 1. I have no known tie to Buchwald, Hartwig or Kosugi (my mentor was Masamune, not a candidate). I am a Lund University colleague of Heiner Linke and Emma Sparr, which the chair has noted and which does not affect any shortlisted candidate. I am the only synthetic organic chemist on the committee, so my preference for a synthesis-methods candidate reflects my field and I have tried to weigh B056 on its merits.
